source: FAO/OIE/World Bank, "Good Practices for Biosecurity in the Pig Sector - Issues and Options in Developing and Transition Countries", FAO Animal Production and Health Paper No. 169, Rome, 2010.
text: Vehicles that move between pig farms (feed delivery trucks, pig transport vehicles, technician or trader vehicles) are a recognized route for carrying disease on manure-contaminated tyres and bodywork, so where practical: unload feed and load/unload pigs at the edge of the farm rather than letting vehicles drive up to the pens; do not allow drivers to enter the pig housing itself; and clean vehicles thoroughly before they visit another farm. For visitors and workers, ask whether they have recently visited another pig farm, slaughterhouse or market before letting them near the pigs, since this is one of the most common ways disease is carried between farms by people rather than animals.
